nodes.name: MgMOF-74 Synthesis
nodes.procedure: Mg(NO3)2·6H2O (0.4 g) and 2,5-dihydroxy benzene carboxylic acid (0.09 g) were mixed and dissolved in 40 mL of N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF). A mixture of ethanol, water, and triethylamine mixtures (9:9:1, v/v/v) was added to the above solution and stirred for 3 h at room temperature. The resulting MgMOFs were collected by centrifugation and then redispersed in DMF. The suspension was treated at 100°C for 2 h to dissolve other amorphous impurities.

nodes.name: Pt/MgO Synthesis
nodes.procedure: In a typical procedure, a mixture of 50 mg of MgMOF and 3 mL of aqueous H2PtCl6 solution (10 mg/mL) was dissolved in 8 mL of deionized water and ultrasonically treated for 10 min. After magnetic stirring for 24 h at room temperature, the precipitates were collected by centrifugation and then freeze-dried to obtain the precursor. The precursor was then placed into a tube furnace and heated to 700°C in a mixture of oxygen and nitrogen (O2:N2 = 5:95) for 4 h at a heating rate of 10°C/min to obtain the desired Pt/MgO.

nodes.characterization_summary: Diffraction peaks at 2θ = 39.8° and 46.4° indexed to (111) and (200) planes of fcc Pt nanocrystals, other peaks correspond to MgO support.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The successful synthesis of Pt/MgO is confirmed by powder X-ray diffraction (XRD) as shown in Fig. 1a. The diffraction peaks at 2θ angles of 39.8° and 46.4° are indexed to the (111) and (200) planes of fcc Pt nanocrystals, respectively...

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows uniform dispersion of Pt nanoparticles (~5 nm) on MgO nanosheet support.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1b presents a transmission electron microscopy (TEM) image of Pt/MgO, indicating the uniform dispersion of Pt nanoparticles on the MgO nanosheet support... The sizes of the Pt nanoparticles are ~5 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice fringes of 0.196 nm and 0.209 nm ascribed to (200) planes of fcc Pt and (200) plane of MgO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From the high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image in Fig. 1c, the lattice fringes of 0.196 and 0.209 nm are ascribed to the (200) planes of fcc Pt and (200) plane of MgO, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping reveals Pt nanoparticles homogeneously dispersed on MgO support.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) mapping qualitatively reveals that the Pt nanoparticles are homogeneously dispersed on the MgO support (Fig. 1d).

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM shows majority of Pt/MgO and MgO nanosheets are 200–500 nm in width and ~4 nm in thickness.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From the atomic force microscopy (AFM) images as shown in Supplementary Fig. 4, a majority of the Pt/MgO nanosheets are approximately 200–500 nm in width and ~4 nm in thickness.

nodes.characterization_summary: EXAFS fitting shows Pt first shell coordination number of 10.1, significantly lower than Pt foil (12).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EXAFS fitting results (Supplementary Fig. 6 and Table 1) show that the coordination number of the first shell of Pt is 10.1, which is significantly lower than the value (12) of Pt foil.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt content in Pt/MgO samples is 3.2 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy (ICP–AES) analysis reveals that the content of Pt in the Pt/MgO samples is 3.2 wt%.

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR shows strong signal at g = 2.00 arising from oxygen vacancies (Vo) in both Pt/MgO and MgO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EPR spectra of both Pt/MgO and MgO (Supplementary Fig. 13) show a strong signal at g = 2.00 arising from oxygen vacancies (Vo), suggesting a high concentration of vo in both the MgO and Pt/MgO.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt 4f7/2 XPS spectrum shows peaks at 71.4 eV (Pt0) and 70.6 eV (Ptδ-), confirming negatively-charged Pt atoms.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Pt 4f7/2 XPS spectrum of Pt/MgO can be deconvoluted into two peaks at 71.4 and 70.6 eV. The 71.4 eV peak is ascribed to the Pt0 state... The 70.6 eV peak... can arise only from negatively-charged Pt atoms (Ptδ-).

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt L3-edge XANES shows slightly weaker white line at ~11568 eV than Pt foil, indicating higher 5d occupancy and Ptδ- state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The slightly weaker white line of Pt/MgO relative to that of Pt foil thus indicates the higher 5d occupancy of Pt, in agreement with the existence of Ptδ- therein.
